jobs.cover_letter:
Dear Hiring Manager,

I am applying for the Paralegal role at Global University Systems because the in-house legal context genuinely interests me, and my background in case management, document review, legal research and client-facing advice maps directly onto what the role requires.

At Bryan Cave Leighton Paisner, I spent a year supporting complex disputes across international arbitration and real estate litigation. In arbitration, I reviewed and organised evidence, amended sections of a claimant's memorial, drafted procedural orders and procedural histories, and coordinated documents across an international team under significant deadline pressure. When I became the only junior supporting the team shortly before a major submission, I tracked outstanding actions across multiple workstreams and helped ensure the filing went out on time. That experience gave me a clear picture of what organised, deadline-driven case management actually looks like in practice.

Since July 2026, I have been advising clients at Citizens Advice East Berkshire on welfare, housing, employment and debt matters. Each matter involves taking detailed factual statements, identifying the relevant legal issues, drafting correspondence, preparing document schedules and maintaining confidential case records from instruction through to submission. Translating complex procedural rules into clear, practical guidance for people in difficult circumstances has sharpened my ability to communicate legal issues accessibly, which I expect would be useful in an in-house team dealing with colleagues and stakeholders who are not legally trained.

My academic work is also relevant. I hold a 2:1 LLB from UCL and an LLM in Comparative and International Dispute Resolution from Queen Mary, where I studied legal research, evidence analysis and international procedural law. My dissertation examined data protection law across jurisdictions, and a separate taught module on data privacy and governance received a mark of 75.

GUS operates across multiple jurisdictions and institutions, and the legal team's work will span a wide range of issues touching on regulatory compliance, contracts and institutional governance. That breadth is exactly what I am looking to develop into at paralegal level, building on the foundation I have in research, case management and drafting.

Yours sincerely,
Maria Silva

jobs.cover_letter:
Dear Hiring Manager,

I am applying for the Litigation Legal Assistant role in Bexleyheath because litigation support is where my practical experience is strongest, and this role offers the kind of varied caseload exposure that I want to build on at this stage of my career.

My most relevant experience is the year I spent at Bryan Cave Leighton Paisner, where I supported two litigation teams across international arbitration and real estate disputes. In the arbitration rotation, I became the only junior supporting the team shortly before a significant submission deadline. That meant coordinating documents across the matter, tracking outstanding actions and helping ensure everything was filed on time, which is directly comparable to the file and deadline management this role involves. I also maintained structured electronic case files throughout, and liaised with the client about required documents and with an external translator about Romanian-language materials. In the real estate disputes rotation, I prepared electronic hearing bundles, assisted with skeleton arguments, conducted legal research on leasehold and landlord and tenant issues, and handled matter opening and closure using iManage.

At Citizens Advice, I have continued developing the client-facing side of legal support. I take detailed factual statements from clients, prepare correspondence and document schedules, and manage matters from first instruction through to submission while keeping accurate case records. Many of my clients are in difficult circumstances, so translating procedural requirements into plain, practical guidance is a regular part of the work.

I am drawn to this role because a busy litigation department with a varied caseload is the environment where I have consistently learned the most. Working across different matter types at BCLP showed me how quickly exposure to a range of disputes builds both legal understanding and practical confidence, and I want to continue developing in that kind of setting. My LLM in Comparative and International Dispute Resolution, which I am completing this year at Queen Mary, sits alongside that practical background rather than replacing it.

I would welcome the opportunity to discuss my application further.

Yours sincerely,
Maria Silva

Dear Hiring Manager,

I am applying for the Knowledge Paralegal role in A&O Shearman's Global Financial Markets Group. My interest in financial markets work developed from a specific point. At the A&O Shearman open day in August 2026, a session on private equity transactions and a workshop on lender security, including examples involving aircraft and ship financing, gave me a concrete picture of how legal work shapes market practice at the transactional level. I followed that up by completing a Coursera course on private equity, studying fund structures, leverage and exit strategies, because I wanted to understand the commercial mechanics that sit behind the legal documentation. That progression is why a knowledge-focused role in GFM is the right next step for me, not a generic ambition.

My research and writing skills have been tested in contexts that translate directly to knowledge work. At BCLP, across a year-long placement in international arbitration and real estate disputes, I drafted procedural histories, amended sections of a claimant's memorial and prepared procedural orders. I also conducted legal and factual research on easements, leasehold issues and rights of light, writing up findings in a form the fee-earner could use immediately. At Q-Legal, I produced a formal written advice letter on UK GDPR obligations for a data-driven start-up, translating statutory requirements into commercially focused guidance under a solicitor's supervision. Both roles required me to frame legal analysis clearly for a specific audience rather than reproduce the law in the abstract.

Organising and maintaining structured materials under pressure is something I have done consistently. At BCLP I became the sole junior supporting an arbitration team shortly before a significant submission deadline, coordinating documents, tracking outstanding actions and helping ensure on-time filing. At Citizens Advice I now manage matters from instruction to submission, maintaining confidential case records and meeting deadlines across a varied caseload. I understand that knowledge work depends on that same discipline applied to resources and outputs the wider team relies on.

A&O Shearman is where the interest started, and this role is a direct extension of that.

Yours sincerely,
Maria Silva
